title: Anyone have insight into AI decompilation?
author: Weird_Point_4262
selftext: Figured I'd check if anyone here has tried it before I just throw game files at Claude or codex. Which is better between the two at it? Any tricks I should know? How long does it take and how many tokens?

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: The older the game the easier time you'll have. I've added literally an entire new game mode to wwe 13, for example, but have a hard time adding basic features to wwe 26. Claude

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
It requires tens of thousands of tokens and thousands of real world dollars.

And it only works with games that can actually have their contents dumped, which usually means older titles and - in particular - old roms. There's a reason all of the footage of the mash-ups are from ancient games - people are dumping rom files into Claude or Astra. Rom files by their very nature are easy to rip code and assets from because they're already decompiled dumps of a binary.

So, small indie games without meaningful copy protection or encryption, old games, rom files... and that's about it. If you want, you can spend $10K putting Max Payne into Super Smash Bros, except not really, just the Max Payne skin over Donkey Kong's bones or whatever.

IMHO, there are much more affordable tricks one can do if the aim is to impress children, which is all this kind of thing really does.
